definition.description: Patient-reported role functioning score from the EORTC QLQ-C30 quality of life instrument.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value for 'Role Function' (or 'Role') from the EORTC QLQ-C30 assessment. If the score is reported as a fraction (e.g., '70/100'), extract the numerator.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the EORTC QLQ-C30 Role Function score is not documented or is ambiguous.
definition.name: qlq_c30_role_function

definition.description: Presence of a history of radiation therapy prior to the current treatment phase.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify any documentation indicating the patient has undergone radiation therapy, including external-beam radiation therapy (EBRT), stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT), or general radiation therapy procedures.
definition.missing_value_rule: If radiation therapy is not mentioned, is explicitly documented as unknown, or is ambiguous, it is represented as 'No'.
definition.name: radiation_therapy_history

definition.description: The total number of radiation therapy sessions received by the patient prior to the baseline measurement.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric count of radiation therapy treatments or sessions documented in the patient's pretreatment clinical records.
definition.missing_value_rule: If no numeric count of radiation therapy sessions is documented or the information is ambiguous, represent as null.
definition.name: radiation_therapy_session_count

definition.description: History of radiosurgery or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) prior to the pretreatment record.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient record contains any mention of prior radiosurgery or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), including terms such as 'post-srs' or specific SRS dosing (e.g., 'srs 12 gy').
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if there is no mention of radiosurgery; represent as null if the documentation specifically suggests the history is unknown or ambiguous.
definition.name: radiosurgery_history

definition.description: The patient's ability to touch their toes, reflecting lower back and hamstring range of motion.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is documented as able or unable to touch their toes during a physical examination.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the ability to touch toes is not documented or is ambiguous.
definition.name: range_of_motion_touch_toes

definition.description: Binary indicator of whether a rash is present in the patient's clinical record.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify whether the pretreatment records explicitly mention the presence of a rash or rashes.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Absent' if no mention of a rash is found or if the documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: rash_presence

definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient's pretreatment record indicates the presence of a skin rash or pruritus (itching).
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if there is no mention of rash or pruritus in the patient record.
definition.name: rash_pruritus_presence

definition.description: Serum creatinine level used as a proxy for renal function status.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value of serum creatinine from the pretreatment record, typically found within a renal panel.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if serum creatinine is not documented or is ambiguous.
definition.name: renal_function_status

definition.description: The number of breaths taken by the patient per minute.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value for respiratory rate (RR) from the vital signs section of the pretreatment clinical record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the respiratory rate is not documented or is provided only as a non-numeric description.
definition.name: respiratory_rate

themes.disagreements: Radiographic features exhibit a spectrum of roles: PET metrics (164, 168), metastasis location (216), and optic chiasm enhancement (235) show dual roles as confounders and modifiers; pulmonary imaging (273, 276) predominantly predicts treatment; whereas cranial features (304, 310) strongly indicate effect heterogeneity.
themes.interpretation: Comprehensive radiographic imaging findings ranging from purely prognostic and predictive of treatment to robust evidence of treatment-effect modification.
themes.name: Comprehensive Radiographic Imaging

themes.disagreements: Pharmacotherapy agents range from clear confounders (lisinopril 209) to dual roles for line of therapy (184) and prior immunotherapy (169); radiation session count (281) predicts treatment while radiosurgery (282) is primarily prognostic.
themes.interpretation: Prior systemic therapies and procedural history that drive both treatment assignment (confounding) and treatment-effect modification.
themes.name: Systemic and Procedural Therapy History

themes.disagreements: Symptomatic burden and PROs (269, 270, 278, 279) are dominant predictors of both treatment and outcome; conversely, metabolic response (215) and pain management (217) show a stronger shift toward effect modification.
themes.interpretation: Patient-reported outcomes and clinical performance metrics acting as powerful prognostic factors with evidence for treatment heterogeneity.
themes.name: Clinical Performance and Patient-Reported Metrics

themes.disagreements: High-confidence confounders include knee osteoarthritis (177), respiratory rate (287), and bone density (239); however, serum chemistry (295, 299) and systemic health markers (259, 260) show evidence of effect modification.
themes.interpretation: Systemic physiological vitals and organ-function markers that serve as primary drivers of treatment selection and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Systemic Vitals and Organ-Level Health

themes.disagreements: Robust prognostic signals for rash/pruritus (285) and transependymal flow (326) contrast with weak signals for skeletal fractures (303) and bilirubin (336); smoking cessation (307) shows stronger treatment prediction than smoking status (306).
themes.interpretation: Patient-level factors ranging from demographics and systemic health to cutaneous symptoms, primarily serving as prognostic factors or predictors for treatment assignment.
themes.name: Patient Demographics and Systemic Health Status

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
